title: Multimodal Integration After Stroke
summary: The study examines multisensory integration (the processing of different sensory perceptions, e.g. seeing and hearing simultaneously) after a stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA) in comparison with healthy individuals. Since many patients struggle to combine sensory information, the influence of the brain areas affected by the stroke and the cognitive functions on perception, cognitive flexibility, and reaction times is analyzed.  The goal is to identify potential deficits and develop new approaches for targeted rehabilitation.
conditions: Stroke, not specified as haemorrhage or infarction
Transient cerebral ischaemic attacks and related syndromes

interventions.name:
Stroke (Thalamic Infarction, Middle Cerebral Artery Infarction, Posterior Cerebral Artery Infarction)
Medical history, neurological and cognitive testing at a time of examination 2-4 days after stroke

Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA)
Medical history, neurological and cognitive testing at a time of examination 2-4 days after TIA

Healthy control subjects
Medical history, neurological and cognitive testing at a time of examination

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Capacity to consent
- Thalamic, posterior, or middle cerebral artery infarction
- Transient ischemic attack (TIA)
- Healthy control
Exclusion criteria:
- Current psychiatric or acute infectious neurological disease
- Dyslexia
- Drug use, excessive alcohol consumption
- Deafness or cochlear implant
- Blindness
- Current use of antipsychotic or seizure-suppressing medication
- Delirium
- Dementia
